title: Towards a Dynamic and Fixed-budget Memory Bank for Efficient Streaming Video Understanding
topic: CausalMem: online redundancy reduction under a fixed token bank
review_depth: abstract; method; setup; conclusion; Appendix A/B targeted full-text review; selective review, not all lines/appendices
contribution: Training-free fixed-budget visual memory maintained with an evolving orthonormal semantic basis.
retention_or_core_mechanism: Basis-relative novelty/redundancy drives online retention; no future query required.
evaluation_scope: StreamingBench and OVO-Bench; offline VideoMME, LongVideoBench, MLVU, LVBench; LLaVA-OneVision and Qwen2.5-VL.
author_stated_limitations: Appendix A, PDF p13: frozen-backbone visual perception, temporal reasoning and instruction-following constrain performance; stronger backbones proposed.
analyst_observed_limits: Inference: semantic residual energy can be an imperfect proxy for a short, low-energy but task-critical cue. This failure is a hypothesis, not established by the paper.
candidate_gaps: Compare semantic novelty against causal-query fidelity on brief evidence and scene changes at equal budget.
already_addressed_by: Implemented online semantic-basis novelty already addresses generic semantic-diversity retention.
cheap_test: Replay a short delayed-cue stream, log cue survival and maintenance cost; avoid a full benchmark until mechanism differs.

title: ObjectStream: Latent Objects as Memory Anchors for Streaming Video Understanding
topic: Latent object anchors and bounded histories
review_depth: abstract; object-anchor mechanism; experimental setup p5; conclusion targeted review; selective review, not all lines/appendices
contribution: Training-free object-centric memory without external detectors or segmentation.
retention_or_core_mechanism: Spatially coherent frozen representations form cross-frame object anchors; preserve persistent histories, transient residuals and a recent window.
evaluation_scope: Qwen2.5-VL-3B/7B; StreamingBench and OVO-Bench; EgoSchema and VideoMME-Long. PDF p5: online 1 fps, at most 256 frames, 64 objects with 8 tokens/object; offline protocol uses larger budgets.
author_stated_limitations: No dedicated author-limitations passage identified in targeted review; do not treat absence of a section as absence of limitations.
analyst_observed_limits: Inference: cross-frame association errors and evaluation beyond the reported online frame cap need controlled measurement.
candidate_gaps: Identity-switch and transient-state survival at fixed byte budget; distinguish persistent entities from absence-based scene states.
already_addressed_by: Implemented object histories and transient-change memory close a generic claim that object-aware bounded memory is missing. MEMO offers a second, externally detected variant.
cheap_test: Construct/reuse an identity-switch clip and measure retained event evidence and QA before expensive runs.

title: StreamFlow: Dynamic Memory Flows for Streaming Video Understanding
topic: Dynamic memory access and attention-guided latent injection
review_depth: abstract; sections 3.1-3.4 (attention-guided injection §3.4, PDF pp5-6, VAS eq8); evaluation setup and causal protocol; conclusion; selective full-text review
contribution: Combines pre-encoder dynamics filtering, trained latent memory and generation-time retrieval.
retention_or_core_mechanism: Pixel/GOP dynamics filters mid-term frames; latent compressor consolidates history; weak visual reliance during generation triggers injection of historical visual latents.
evaluation_scope: Qwen3.5-9B backbone with trained/LoRA memory compressor and teacher-generated supervision; StreamingBench plus MVBench, MLVU and VideoMME; explicit causal frame/query protocol.
author_stated_limitations: No dedicated author-limitations statement identified in selected sections.
analyst_observed_limits: Inference: training data and compressor training make full reproduction a poor default for one rented GPU for a few days; generation-time retrieval cost and false triggers must be budgeted.
candidate_gaps: Compare calibrated retrieval decisions under matched overhead; any new trigger needs gains beyond existing attention-guided injection.
already_addressed_by: Implemented generation-time attention-guided historical visual injection directly overlaps generic entropy/attention-triggered evidence reinjection.
cheap_test: Use checkpoint if available; first measure existing trigger precision on a small set rather than train a compressor.

title: StreamTTT: Reconciling Real-Time Perception and Long-Term Memory in Streaming VLMs
topic: Learned fast-weight long-term memory plus recent KV
review_depth: abstract; introduction mechanism and training; benchmark table/protocol targeted review; selective review, not all lines/appendices
contribution: Separates long history from attention context through online-updated fast weights.
retention_or_core_mechanism: Gated test-time-training memory branch stores historical state; short sliding KV serves present perception; jointly trained on offline and real-time QA.
evaluation_scope: StreamTTT-4B; OVO-Bench perception/backward tracing and StreamingBench RTVU; comparisons explicitly under each reported input protocol.
author_stated_limitations: No dedicated author-limitations passage identified in targeted review.
analyst_observed_limits: Inference: training and architecture changes exceed a simple drop-in cache patch; per-paper protocol differences prevent treating headline scores as matched evidence.
candidate_gaps: Training-free approximation of the recent/long-memory tradeoff needs direct controls; architecture equivalence cannot be assumed.
already_addressed_by: Implemented fast-weight/short-KV separation closes broad claims that separating recent perception from long memory is new.
cheap_test: Only compare with released weights under matching input/timestamp conditions; gate on memory and inference compatibility.

title: Dynamic Hub-and-Spoke Memory for Streaming Video Understanding
topic: D-HSM structured textual evidence and entity retrieval
review_depth: abstract; memory/retrieval description; section 7 author limitations p10; selective review, not all lines/appendices
contribution: Training-free entity-linked textual distant memory with recent visual evidence.
retention_or_core_mechanism: Typed observations form entity hubs and evidence spokes; query-aware retrieval and graph expansion select historical text.
evaluation_scope: Streaming and long-video benchmarks with frozen VLM backbones; distant history represented textually.
author_stated_limitations: Section 7, PDF p10: entity recognition/OCR/action errors can propagate into memory; text can lose fine-grained distant detail; robust entity linking left for future work.
analyst_observed_limits: Inference: author-admitted propagated observation error supports a reliability/provenance diagnostic, but does not establish that a proposed remedy is novel.
candidate_gaps: How to prevent incorrect generated memory from steering future selection while preserving useful historical conditioning?
already_addressed_by: Implemented entity-graph retrieval overlaps generic structured memory. Robust entity linking is proposed future work, not an implemented solution.
cheap_test: Inject one controlled wrong textual observation and compare downstream retrieval/evidence survival with history masked.

title: KeyRec: Bounded Visual Memory for Streaming and Long-Video Understanding
topic: Bounded add-merge-evict event memory with query-adaptive readout
review_depth: abstract; add-merge-evict/router mechanism; Appendix E limitations p17; selective review, not all lines/appendices
contribution: Separates query-agnostic construction from query-adaptive fixed-budget visual readout.
retention_or_core_mechanism: Recent cache plus novel event proposals, similarity/time consolidation and add-merge-evict; text-only query router allocates recent/event read budget.
evaluation_scope: Four benchmarks and three backbones including Gemma 4 E2B/E4B and NEO-ov 2B; post-encoder visual memory and decoder cost.
author_stated_limitations: Appendix E, PDF p17: fixed update/routing rules; no ViT encoding savings; attempted intermediate token reduction disrupted optimized path with no wall-time gain; lacks explicit identity/trajectory/state modeling.
analyst_observed_limits: Inference: combining encoding compression with memory must be measured end to end; lower token count alone does not establish speed.
candidate_gaps: Can native-path-compatible maintenance reduce wall time and retain brief evidence at constant budget?
already_addressed_by: Implemented bounded event organization and query router already exist. ObjectStream/MEMO implement some object directions merely proposed by KeyRec; learning update rules remains future work here.
cheap_test: Profile encoder, decoder, update and decode costs separately; compare one compatible encoder optimization on identical clips.

title: MEMO: Multi-Level Entity-Aware Memory for Streaming Video Understanding
topic: Entity-aware chunk indices with visual evidence retrieval
review_depth: abstract; memory mechanism; experimental settings; section 5 limitations p8; selective review, not all lines/appendices
retention_or_core_mechanism: Detection/segmentation/association inform coherent chunks; lightweight indices retrieve high-resolution visual evidence from a separate CPU pool.
evaluation_scope: StreamingBench and OVO-Bench; LLaVA-OV-0.5B/7B, Qwen2.5-VL-7B and Qwen3-VL-8B; 1 fps; top3 chunks; 16 frame visual input split recent/retrieved.
author_stated_limitations: Section 5, PDF p8: upstream detector/segmenter/association errors propagate; implicit/absence-based states poorly represented; persistent cross-chunk identity and hour/day consolidation remain open; explicit scene-state memory/reranking/consolidation future work.
analyst_observed_limits: Inference: bounded model input is distinct from bounded total CPU/raw-evidence storage; require growth accounting before claiming all-memory bounds.
candidate_gaps: Absence/state-transition evidence and persistent error correction are specific comparative questions; hour/day consolidation is high-cost for this project.
already_addressed_by: Implemented entity-aware chunk retrieval and object dynamics overlap generic object-memory claims. Explicit absence/state memory is stated future work, not solved by that statement.
cheap_test: Small clips with object leaving, occlusion and true absence; compare with an entity-memory baseline and report false absence.

title: ReMem: Streaming Video Understanding With Long Context Retention
topic: Recursive compressed context plus retrieved vision memory
review_depth: abstract; SCM/RVM and GQC method pp3-4; experiments p5; selective review, not all lines/appendices
contribution: Training-free adaptation combines fixed-length context state and question-conditioned vision retrieval.
retention_or_core_mechanism: SCM recursively compresses previous context plus new visual tokens using GQC; RVM selects question-relevant tokens by cosine similarity and reinjects them into context.
evaluation_scope: LLaVA-OV-7B and Qwen2.5-VL-7B; StreamingBench contextual SQA/MCU/ACU, OVO EPM/ASI/HLD; EgoSchema and VideoMME.
author_stated_limitations: No dedicated author-limitations passage identified in targeted review.
analyst_observed_limits: Inference: repeated compression can create irreversible loss, and fixed SCM size alone does not prove bounded whole-system RVM storage.
candidate_gaps: Compression-depth/cue-survival stress test with matched complete memory accounting.
already_addressed_by: Implemented fixed compressed context and query-driven visual reinjection overlap generic recall/reinjection ideas; ProtoKV separately studies delayed queries.
cheap_test: Measure answer stability and evidence survival after repeated irrelevant chunks, keeping query semantics fixed.

title: Memory: A Contribution to Experimental Psychology
review_depth: two-page extracted text and bibliographic header review; selective review, not all lines/appendices
contribution: Historical account of memory experiments; conceptual context only.
retention_or_core_mechanism: Human learning/retention experiments; no computational KV retention mechanism.
evaluation_scope: Two-page 2013 Annals of Neurosciences reprint of historical Ebbinghaus work/translation.
author_stated_limitations: Not applicable to modern computational-method claims; no transformer/KV limitations claimed.
analyst_observed_limits: Inference: a biological analogy supplies motivation but no evidence of machine-learning novelty or algorithmic superiority.
candidate_gaps: No original HERMES method gap can be inferred from this source alone.
cheap_test: Not applicable; use empirical computational controls instead.

title: HERMES: KV Cache as Hierarchical Memory for Efficient Streaming Video Understanding
topic: Layer-wise hierarchical KV retention, smoothing and position reindexing
review_depth: abstract; method architecture; experimental setup p6; targeted limitation search; selective review, not all lines/appendices
contribution: Training-free hierarchical cache management motivated by layer-wise attention behavior.
retention_or_core_mechanism: Shallow recency, deep anchors, middle transition; cross-layer smoothing and RoPE-aware position reindexing; direct reuse at query arrival.
evaluation_scope: PDF p6: StreamingBench, OVO-Bench, RVS-Ego/Movie; MVBench, VideoMME and EgoSchema; LLaVA-OV and Qwen2.5-VL spanning 0.5B-32B; A800 efficiency tests.
author_stated_limitations: No dedicated author-limitations section identified in targeted review. Do not attribute local scorer defects to the authors without official-code/version comparison.
analyst_observed_limits: Inference: project baseline has an inconclusive 4K advantage and a local proxy/native-attention mismatch; correcting implementation is a validity prerequisite, not original contribution.
candidate_gaps: After correction, test cached causal scoring with refresh controls and error-feedback sensitivity against fixed native scoring.
already_addressed_by: Same underlying work as local 2026.acl-long.381.pdf (version overlap; not necessarily identical bytes). Hierarchical retention itself is existing HERMES.
cheap_test: Small paired corrected-scorer pilot with identical memory budget, then method ablations only if benefit survives.

title: OASIS: On-Demand Hierarchical Event Memory for Streaming Video Reasoning
topic: Hierarchical event forest and selective historical recall
review_depth: abstract; section 3 event-forest formulation; motivation p2 and conclusion; selective review, not all lines/appendices
contribution: On-demand event-level temporal routing through multi-resolution event memory.
retention_or_core_mechanism: High-fidelity short window, medium buffer, event forest with timestamps/frames/generated summaries/embeddings; short context first and selective distant retrieval.
evaluation_scope: Streaming-video reasoning evaluation; detailed numerical comparability must be checked against actual protocol, not inferred from headline results.
author_stated_limitations: No dedicated author-limitations passage identified in targeted review.
analyst_observed_limits: Inference: generated summaries/retrieval may introduce persistent errors; distinguish GPU context bounds from retained frame and text storage.
candidate_gaps: Specific reliability/feedback or calibrated abstention diagnostic may remain comparative; generic uncertainty-triggered history recall is already implemented.
already_addressed_by: Implemented on-demand short/long event routing overlaps broad EDMI-style historical recall. StreamFlow also implements generation-time visual injection.
cheap_test: Compare no retrieval, always retrieval and existing selective retrieval on matched context/latency before designing a new trigger.

title: ProtoKV: Streaming Video Understanding under Delayed Query with Summary-State Memory
topic: Bounded summary-state memory and delayed-query evaluation
review_depth: abstract; summary-state mechanism; section 4.1 delayed-query protocol p6; conclusion; selective review, not all lines/appendices
contribution: Keeps exact near context and compressed object-centric prototype/residual state for far history.
retention_or_core_mechanism: Spatial/semantic prototypes plus residual statistics exposed as bounded pseudo-tokens, rather than selecting only old token instances.
evaluation_scope: Four streaming benchmarks; controlled delayed-query sweeps using dataset timestamp t0; retrospective-type filter and common valid-query intersection (section 4.1 p6).
author_stated_limitations: Section 4.1, p6 explicitly notes no ground-truth last-evidence time te; delay is measured from dataset query timestamp t0 instead. Conclusion leaves richer summaries/broader streaming settings to future work.
analyst_observed_limits: Inference: timestamp-delay sweeps are weaker than annotated last-evidence-delay tests; cue timing needs verification for precise retention claims.
candidate_gaps: Evidence-anchored delay and contamination robustness are more precise than generic delayed-query memory.
already_addressed_by: Implemented bounded summary state and controlled delayed-query experiments directly overlap broad delayed-evidence retention novelty.
cheap_test: Use a few clips with known decisive cue time; retrospective answers only; compare matched query sets across delays.

title: Decouple and Cache: KV Cache Construction for Streaming Video Understanding
topic: DSCache position-agnostic past memory and instant recent context
review_depth: abstract; section 3 and figure 2 p4; conclusion section 6; selective review, not all lines/appendices
contribution: Training-free decoupling of cumulative past cache from on-demand recent cache construction.
retention_or_core_mechanism: Store pre-RoPE keys; small FIFO feature buffer supplies independently constructed recent/instant cache; combine with cumulative past cache for QA.
evaluation_scope: Streaming-video QA; recent-context construction incurs query-time work; numeric comparisons require matching input and budget.
author_stated_limitations: Conclusion section 6 proposes faster instant-cache construction and better past-cache optimization as future work.
analyst_observed_limits: Inference: pre-RoPE decoupling solves a positional/cache-construction concern but does not itself establish query-state freshness or correctness of local scorer.
candidate_gaps: Amortized causal scoring versus on-demand recent reconstruction is a cost/quality comparison, not proof of novel cache decoupling.
already_addressed_by: Implemented position-agnostic cache and recent/past separation; related pre-RoPE safety also Video-MemComp.
cheap_test: Time first query and repeated queries separately with identical recent buffer and total byte budget.

title: Accelerating Streaming Video Large Language Models via Hierarchical Token Compression
topic: STC encoder feature caching plus prefill pruning
review_depth: abstract; section 3 compressors; contribution list p2; conclusion; selective review, not all lines/appendices
contribution: Training-free compression spanning vision encoder and LLM prefill.
retention_or_core_mechanism: STC-Cacher reuses adjacent-frame visual features; STC-Pruner removes low-saliency tokens while respecting causal unknown-future-query streaming.
evaluation_scope: Streaming VideoLLMs, including ReKV; efficiency and task-quality evaluation.
author_stated_limitations: No dedicated author-limitations passage identified in targeted review.
analyst_observed_limits: Inference: high redundancy and end-to-end bottleneck placement determine benefit; report hit rate and wall time, not only token reduction.
candidate_gaps: Can compatible feature reuse help the actual HERMES profile without compounding retention errors?
already_addressed_by: Implemented causal ViT caching and prefill compression close generic proposals to cache adjacent frames for streaming speed.
cheap_test: Profile first, then test one encoder-cache setting on identical videos with full wall-clock timing.

title: MuKV: Multi-Grained KV Cache Compression for Long Streaming Video Question-Answering
topic: Multi-grain compressed historical KV with retrieval/reranking
review_depth: abstract; compression/retrieval mechanism; section 4.1 p5; conclusion; selective review, not all lines/appendices
contribution: Patch-, frame- and segment-grained historical KV compression and efficient retrieval.
retention_or_core_mechanism: Self-attention/Fourier compression; offline KV storage; grain-agnostic parallel retrieval then hierarchical reranking at query time.
evaluation_scope: Section 4.1 p5: RVS-Ego, RVS-Movie, StreamingBench RTVU subset; metrics online accuracy, efficiency and offline cache storage; changed GPT-3.5 judge version noted.
author_stated_limitations: Section 4.1 p5 discloses original GPT-3.5-turbo-0613 judge was deprecated, so a different GPT-3.5-turbo judge is used; this is an evaluation comparability caveat, not a declared algorithm limitation.
analyst_observed_limits: Inference: storage/retrieval improves recall but is not equivalent to strictly bounded total-memory eviction; judge-version differences can obscure cross-paper score comparisons.
candidate_gaps: Whole-system boundedness and matched-judge controlled recall comparison.
already_addressed_by: Implemented multigrain KV retrieval and reranking overlap generic multiresolution-memory recall.
cheap_test: Report stored bytes versus elapsed stream and use the same answer scorer for any direct comparison.

title: Revisiting Multimodal KV Cache Compression: A Frequency-Domain-Guided Outlier-KV-Aware Approach
topic: Attention-free frequency/outlier scoring with layer-adaptive budgets
review_depth: abstract; scoring/budget mechanism; setup and main evaluation table pp5-6; conclusion; selective review, not all lines/appendices
contribution: Training-free FlashAttention-compatible multimodal cache compression without attention scores.
retention_or_core_mechanism: Frequency-domain outlier key/value signals drive token retention and layer budget assignment.
evaluation_scope: MileBench temporal/semantic multi-image, needle retrieval and image retrieval tasks; LLaVA-OV-1.5-8B, Qwen2.5-VL-7B/32B (section 4.1 pp5-6).
author_stated_limitations: No dedicated author-limitations passage identified in targeted review.
analyst_observed_limits: Inference: offline multimodal evaluation alone does not establish causal unknown-question streaming performance; backbone and policy must be controlled.
candidate_gaps: Compare cheap outlier scoring with causal-state scoring in the same streaming retention policy.
already_addressed_by: Implemented attention-free scoring and layer-adaptive budget allocation; broad cheap-score/adaptive-layer-budget novelty is occupied.
cheap_test: Hold budget, policy and selected token granularity fixed; swap only signal on a small streaming replay.

title: Think-as-You-See: Streaming Chain-of-Thought Reasoning for Large Vision-Language Models
topic: Stream-aligned training and parallel perception/reasoning KV
review_depth: abstract; mechanism overview; section 4.1 p6; conclusion; selective review, not all lines/appendices
contribution: Streaming chain-of-thought with separate perception and reasoning caches.
retention_or_core_mechanism: Parallel-cache design allows perception and progressive reasoning to evolve while frames arrive; trained on stream-aligned reasoning data.
evaluation_scope: Section 4.1 p6: extended VideoEspresso-derived reasoning protocol; Qwen2.5-VL-3B/7B; batch/interleaved and SFT controls; quality and latency.
author_stated_limitations: No dedicated author-limitations passage identified in targeted review.
analyst_observed_limits: Inference: training-dependent reasoning pipeline is a conceptual comparison, not a drop-in baseline for a few-day cache-only improvement.
candidate_gaps: Separate reasoning correctness from retention quality; wrong intermediate reasoning may influence subsequent state and needs explicit diagnostics.
already_addressed_by: Implemented progressive streaming reasoning and dual cache structure overlap generic asynchronous reasoning/cache separation.
cheap_test: If weights available, use one fixed clip and intervene in intermediate reasoning; otherwise keep as conceptual prior art.
